utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But before we adjourn, I'm saying this for the transcript, this is now a Status Conference, and we can conclude in respect to methodology. It's being understood, of course, that you will have all the time necessary to inform your client of all these conversations. Let me point out that a Trial Chamber of this Tribunal has the witness statements given to it, and frequently the Presiding Judge, at least factually, brings in a certain number of questions which it asks the witness. I've never done this because I've never wanted to force the translation service to do more work than it already has to do, that is, to ask all statements be translated into French. But this is a procedure which is covered by the Rules, and I would also be entitled to ask questions myself. It's been understood that after that, the Prosecutor could ask any additional questions he wants. I simply wanted to point this out to you. Before we take any decision, I would like to consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will hope that Mr. Jelisic is feeling better. Here are at least the temporary provisional conclusions that the Judges have reached: The Judges do not wish and do not find in the text material for imposing any method on the Defence should the Defence not accept that method. Nonetheless, the Judges consider that the parties are free to present their cases as they see fit with respect for the full rights of the accused and his Defence attorneys to conduct a proper cross-examination. Having said this, we suggest that the summary which was drafted by the Office of the Prosecutor, and only by that office, should be presented to the witness, that the witness should identify it so that the exhibit be admitted as an exhibit. I'm not speaking about probative value. I'm simply speaking about admission of the exhibit. The Prosecutor will ask questions in the form of observations drawn from the summary. Fourthly, the Defence will have the required time to conduct its cross-examination. The Defence will, however, before the cross-examination, be required to say how long is going to be required for that cross-examination to be conducted, as covered by a flexible interpretation of Rule 90(H), but which will be interpreted, as I say, with flexibility, as we have always done, and so that the Defence does not feel itself constrained to work within a short time should the examination in chief have been very short. That's how we are going to proceed, which will impose nothing on the Defence. We have noted that the Defence does not agree with the way the proceedings are being conducted and therefore will be able to do as it sees fit in its cross-examination, the way it seems appropriate for its strategy. Mr. Prosecutor, could you operate that way starting tomorrow, if we can resume tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly, I will do that. While I'm on my feet, would it be convenient to mention one other administrative matter? The Chamber will recall that there are five witnesses on the list provided to the Defence different from the names on an earlier list. I have to know by, I think, Thursday whether they are to come next week, because although they are willing and able to come, they are still in Bosnia. I think it will help the Chamber if it has some knowledge in advance of what those witnesses may say, and it so happens that there are summaries of those witnesses of a similar kind, but much shorter because the witnesses are shorter in the material that they can give. I think each summary is two sides. I'll provide those to my learned friends this evening, and if it would help the Chamber, I could provide them to your legal officers in the morning in case you had an opportunity to pre-read them before tomorrow afternoon's session, and it would help me if I can, at some stage tomorrow afternoon, argue whether or raise with you whether those witnesses should be called to give evidence. I can simply say that for various reasons, not least that other witnesses who had been available to come are now not available, or one in particular, that it's necessary and desirable to call further evidence. In any event, the way I'm presenting the case, in my judgement, makes it desirable for a little more evidence on one or two topics to be available, and that judgement has been substantially reinforced by the very clear and helpful way Mr. Greaves explained today that notwithstanding everything that's in the interview by way of admissions, that's interview of the defendant, there is no acceptance of any killing beyond those which pleas of guilty have been tendered. That may not have been forecast at an earlier stage when pleas of guilty for murder were taken and when my colleagues, then and present, made the decision about witnesses, but now it's known. Therefore, that's another reason. But I'll flush that out tomorrow. If I can make available to you, either tonight or tomorrow morning, the summaries of what those witnesses can say, as I will to my learned friends, I hope that will be helpful. Whether we argue it or discuss it at 2.00 or at some other stage tomorrow afternoon is a matter, of course, for the Chamber, subject to the observations that my friend may make. If, by chance, the defendant isn't here, I hope that it may be possible at least to discuss those witnesses in his absence because of the travel arrangements that I've already referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Of course, the defendant is not present at the moment, and I don't know what condition he's in. I hope that if it were to turn out that he was sufficiently unwell to be able to attend tomorrow, that an early decision as to whether or not there would be a sitting at all could be taken. If he's available, then of course we can discuss the matters that my learned friend has raised. But in the absence of the defendant, I wouldn't want to commit myself any further than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I suggest that we adjourn and resume tomorrow at 2.00.
